answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable anchor, such as a stake or a device-backed credential that cannot be copied for free. Like a mesa rising above a flat plain, a genuine agent reputation stands out because its history is public and expensive to rebuild. New identities start with limited rights and gain influence only through honest work over a long horizon, so flooding the network with clones buys no power without paying the same cost again for each one.
